profile.summary: DeepSTARR predicts how strongly a 249 base pair piece of DNA acts as an enhancer in Drosophila melanogaster S2 cells. It is a convolutional neural network with two outputs, one for developmental and one for housekeeping enhancer activity, trained on genome-wide UMI-STARR-seq measurements. Besides prediction, it is used to read out which nucleotides drive the predicted activity and so to study transcription factor motifs and their syntax.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: DeepSTARR, DeepSTARR model; preprint abstract; DeepSTARR.model.json: input layer and output layers

summary_quotes.text: **DeepSTARR** is a multi-task convolutional neural network that maps 249 bp long DNA sequences to both their developmental and their housekeeping enhancer activities.
quantitatively predict the activities of developmental and housekeeping enhancers from DNA sequence in *Drosophila melanogaster* S2 cells

Here we built a deep learning model, DeepSTARR, to quantitatively predict the activities of thousands of developmental and housekeeping enhancers directly from DNA sequence in  Drosophila melanogaster S2 cells.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The architecture is adapted from Basset: four convolutional layers, each followed by batch normalisation, a ReLU activation and max pooling, then two fully connected layers of 256 units and two single-unit output layers, Dense_Dev and Dense_Hk. The released model file gives 256 filters of width 7 in the first convolutional layer, then 60 of width 3, 60 of width 5 and 120 of width 3, with pooling size 2 throughout. The convolutional layers pick up local motifs and motif syntax; the fully connected layers combine them into one activity value per enhancer type. The model is a regression on measured UMI-STARR-seq activity, not a classifier.

quotes.text: We adapted the Basset convolutional neural network architecture ([Kelley et al., 2016](https://github.com/davek44/Basset)) and designed DeepSTARR with four convolution layers, each followed by a max-pooling layer, and two fully connected layers.

The convolution layers identify local sequence features (e.g. TF motifs) and increasingly complex patterns (e.g. TF motif syntax), while the fully connected layers combine these features and patterns to predict enhancer activity separately for each enhancer type.

sections.title: Interpreting the model
sections.body: The repository ships a second script that computes nucleotide contribution scores for a given sequence, separately for developmental or housekeeping activity, using DeepLIFT and SHAP. A Colab notebook runs the whole path end to end: training, contribution scores and TF-MoDISco motifs. The preprint states that the model learned TF motifs and higher-order syntax rules, including the effect of motif-flanking sequence and inter-motif distances, and that these rules were validated experimentally.
sections.source_locator: DeepSTARR/README.md: Interpreting DeepSTARR with nucleotide contribution scores, Tutorial; preprint abstract

quotes.text: python DeepSTARR_nucl_contr_scores.py -m DeepSTARR.model -s Sequences_example.fa -c dev # Contribution scores for developmental enhancer activity
An end-to-end example to train DeepSTARR, compute the nucleotide contribution scores and modisco TF motifs is contained in the following colab notebook

The model learned relevant TF motifs and higher-order syntax rules, including functionally non-equivalent instances of the same TF motif that are determined by motif-flanking sequence and inter-motif distances.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One trained model is released, as the Keras pair DeepSTARR.model.json and DeepSTARR.model.h5 on Zenodo record 5502060, published on 2021-09-20 under CC BY 4.0. The same record holds the train, validation and test sequences and their measured activities, so the published evaluation can be repeated. The model is also deposited in Kipoi. The model file was saved with Keras 2.2.4 on the TensorFlow backend, which matches the conda environment the README asks for.

run_guide.summary: Get the repository at the pinned commit, build the pinned conda environment, download the trained model from Zenodo and predict developmental and housekeeping activity for the bundled example sequences.
prerequisites: conda, to create the environment the README pins: python 3.7, tensorflow 1.14.0, keras 2.2.4.
The README's conda line installs tensorflow 1.14.0 and keras 2.2.4, and offers tensorflow-gpu or keras-gpu as an alternative if using a GPU.
Internet access for the Zenodo model files and for the shap fork installed from GitHub.
Code is MIT licensed; the Zenodo record is CC BY 4.0 and open.

notes: The database description for this record was just 'DeepSTARR enhancer activity CNN'. Retrained variants exist (the same author's DeepSTARR_embryo for Drosophila embryo tissues, and third-party mouse versions); only the S2-cell release is described here. The Nature Genetics paper is not openly available at Europe PMC, so the abstract read here is the bioRxiv preprint's. GenBench, the existing source on the record, was not read here; it is a benchmark paper, not the model's own documentation.
